Nyirbogat New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírbogát, Hungary

Not demolished. The newer of two Jewish cemeteries in Nyírbogát, likely established in the 1920s (oldest tombstone dated 1930), remained active until at least 1945. The community, founded around 1840 with 23 members, grew to 404 by 1910 before declining to 298 by 1941; it was never independent, falling first under Balkány's and later Nyírbátor's jurisdiction, and joined the Orthodox stream. Nyírbogát's Jews suffered greatly during the 'White Terror' period; in May 1944, the community was deported to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and then to Auschwitz on May 26.
